# Add exact native place-cycle resident-card continuity witness

## Context

The flagship workstation film gate needs an executable current-head witness for the exact native window journey `1200×1040 → 1000×760 → 1200×1040`, without a drag. The amended parent #16498 names transient resident-card child loss after native restoration, but it deliberately stays open until a historical/native attribution arm and whole-media QA exist.

Two local headed falsifiers on 2026-08-08 established the narrower leaf boundary:

- current styling: 394 sampled rAFs, 6.25 seconds after restoration, zero composition, DOM-identity, disclosure-tier, or settled-containment drift;
- the identical geometry with only the styling declarations introduced by `#16722` removed: 394 sampled rAFs, 6.25 seconds after restoration, also zero drift.

The second result means the isolated styling control did **not** produce the historical signature. It is evidence for `historical attribution NOT PROVEN`, not evidence that `#16722` repaired #16498. What is ready is the executable current-head witness itself.

Duplicate receipt (2026-08-08 21:59Z): live latest 20 open issues, global GitHub search,
Knowledge Base ticket search, repository issue/discussion mirrors, and the latest 30 A2A messages
across all read states contained no equivalent ticket or competing lane claim.

## The Problem

The current E2E suite has no durable oracle for the parent ticket's exact no-drag native place-cycle. Without one, a later flagship run can lose resident-card children or worker/DOM continuity during restoration while the existing tear-out continuity checks stay green.

The missing witness must distinguish three surfaces honestly:

1. live DOM composition and geometry can be sampled on every rAF;
2. config/vdom/vnode identity is observable through Neural Link at explicit station boundaries, not continuously inside browser rAF callbacks;
3. raw child geometry may transiently overrun between disclosure tiers because `.workstation-resident-card` intentionally owns `overflow: clip`; raw containment is therefore a settled-station contract, while presented composition is the transition contract.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL.spec.mjs:120` owns the four resident targets and the continuity suite adjacent to the flagship journey.
- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL.spec.mjs:141` resolves config/vdom/vnode identity through Neural Link.
- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL.spec.mjs:176` is the browser-side rAF sampling seam for live DOM, computed display, clipped presentation, and geometry.
- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/filmStage.mjs:187` owns exact native `Browser.setWindowBounds` placement and its settled-bounds poll.
- `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss:281` makes the card the transient paint boundary; the disclosure ladder begins at line 405.

This is test substrate only. It adds no public API, runtime configuration, or service boundary.

## The Fix

Extend `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL.spec.mjs` with one headed Neural Link witness that:

- places the branded browser at the exact roomy, compact, and restored native bounds;
- samples `Queues`, `Priority Alerts`, `Audit`, and `Commits` on every rAF through the transition and for at least six seconds after restoration;
- derives each declared disclosure tier from computed `display`, records separately which children are actually presented after clipping, and rejects any declared-but-unpresented child or kicker-without-metric frame;
- requires every restored frame whose pane geometry has returned within one pixel of the roomy baseline to declare the baseline child set, so a known-but-wrong `shell` tier cannot false-green a blank roomy card;
- preserves live pane/card DOM node identity and the presence of every resident child across sampled frames;
- records Neural Link config/vdom/vnode identity before the cycle, at compact settle, immediately after restoration, and after the recovery band;
- verifies actual endpoint geometry, pane contraction, restoration parity, settled containment, page errors, and sampler-cap state;
- attaches the full JSON rAF receipt and Playwright video.

## Decision Record impact

none — executable coverage within the landed workstation, Neural Link, and native-placement contracts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exact native `1200×1040 → 1000×760 → 1200×1040` no-drag cycle is exercised through `placeNativeWindow()`.
- [ ] Four resident cards are sampled on every rAF and for at least 6,000 ms after restoration; the sampler must prove it did not hit its frame cap.
- [ ] Every computed-display child set maps to a known disclosure tier; every declared child remains presented; kicker-presented with metric-unpresented reds the witness; restored roomy geometry must declare the roomy baseline child set.
- [ ] Live pane/card DOM identity and all resident child nodes remain present through every sampled frame.
- [ ] Neural Link config/vdom/vnode identity matches at before, compact, restored, and post-band checkpoints.
- [ ] Endpoint outer geometry is exact; all four pane heights contract and restore within one pixel of baseline; raw containment is checked at settled stations only.
- [ ] Page errors, first-drift diagnostics, station geometry, counts, and the full frame stream are attached as JSON; Playwright video remains enabled.
- [ ] The targeted headed E2E spec passes with the custom E2E config.

## Out of Scope

- Closing #16498 or declaring the flagship film complete.
- Claiming historical reproduction or repair attribution to `#16722`.
- Appending the unrelated `1000×420` short-pane station from `#16716`.
- Production CSS, dock projection, tab reconciliation, or pane lifecycle changes.
- Whole-media/human film QA and the external exact-stage triplicate run.

## Avoided Traps

- A `1000×420` control would rediscover the already-known `#16716` short-pane defect, not attribute the exact flagship place-cycle.
- Copying config/vdom ids into every rAF record would make static expectations look like live worker observations.
- Enforcing raw child containment on transition frames would contradict the intentional `overflow: clip` transient contract.
- A green isolated-style control is recorded as non-attribution, never upgraded into a historical red.

- 2026-09-14T18:15:04Z @tobiu referenced in commit `f842523` - "feat(testing): three specs stop keeping private opinions about where a window goes (#18682) (#18698)

* feat(testing): a target can be planned beside an already-placed source (#18682)

Two copies of `placePopupOutsideSource` disagree about what placing a popup outside its source
means. One polls both real rects and moves nothing when they already miss each other, searches four
candidate slots against the available envelope, and throws when none fits. The other offsets by
`innerWidth` — the VIEWPORT width, not the window's outer width — so it under-shoots by the browser
chrome, and under an emulated viewport it offsets by a number that describes no real window at all.
It cannot fail, which makes its misplacement indistinguishable from success.

`planBeside` is the careful copy's candidate search as a pure function, and `rectsOverlap` is the
question a caller asks before deciding to move anything at all. `placeBesideSource` composes them:
the product's own placement gets first refusal, only a genuinely overlapping stage reaches CDP, and
the arrangement itself is asserted at the end rather than inferred from the request having been
accepted.

Refusals are verdicts, not throws, so an impossible display is never discovered halfway through a
gesture. A `moved: false` verdict means the windows were already apart and nothing was touched.

Fourteen arms now cover the planners, including the invariant the blind copy violates: a planned
target never overlaps the source it was planned beside.

The four call sites are not migrated here. They are headed specs and the display is held by another
peer, so migrating them now would mean committing a change I cannot run.

* fix(testing): a stage is planned only against an envelope worth trusting (#18682)

Migrating the first `placePopupOutsideSource` call site walked straight into the defect this lane
exists to prevent, which is the useful part of the exercise.

`DemoBPerspectivesNL` runs under an emulated viewport and emulates `screen` at 1920x1080. Under
emulation `screenX`/`screenY` keep reporting real coordinates while `screen.avail*` reports the
emulation, measured directly: a page reporting a 1280x720 envelope at origin 0,0 while its window
sat on a 3360x1860 display at origin 2056,30. So reading the envelope from an emulated page and
planning against it measures a real window against a stage that does not exist.

`placeBesideSource` now trusts an envelope only when the caller declares one or the page is
unemulated. Otherwise it skips the fit test rather than running it against fiction, places beside
the source, and lets the non-overlap poll be the receipt. That poll was always the real proof; the
fit test is a pre-check, and a pre-check against imaginary bounds is worse than none. The verdict
carries `stageTrusted` so a caller can tell which path ran.

The blind copy this replaces offset by `innerWidth` — the viewport width, not the window's outer
width — with no overlap check, no fit test and no verification, so a misplacement was
indistinguishable from success. The replacement keeps its ability to place and adds the measurement
it never had.

Preservation measured rather than asserted: the spec is red at the base and stays red at the same
`toBe(HOSTED)` assertion, baseline line 168 versus migrated line 144, matching this diff's 24-line
delta exactly. The failure is a cross-window semantic preview the target never settles, untouched
by placement.

Three call sites in `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` remain.

* refactor(testing): the last two placement copies collapse into the shared helper (#18682)

`placePopupOutsideSource` is now zero across the tree: both definitions deleted, all four call
sites on `placeBesideSource`.

The careful copy that dies here was the better of the two, and it still measured its fit test
against `screen.avail*` read from a page running at an emulated 760x720 with `screen` faked to
1920x1080. So its four candidate slots, and the throw when none fitted, were evaluated against a
stage that does not exist. The replacement recognises that case and skips the fit test rather than
running it against fiction, then proves the arrangement by measurement.

What the copy did that survives: the product's own placement keeps first refusal, so a caller that
finds the windows already apart moves nothing; the landing is polled; and the arrangement itself is
asserted at the end rather than inferred from the request being accepted. What it did that does not:
throwing mid-gesture. A refusal is a verdict now, so the caller decides.

Preservation measured on both specs rather than asserted.

  DemoBPerspectivesNL   baseline 1 failed @168  ->  migrated 1 failed @144   (delta 24)
  DemoBCrossWindowDrag  baseline 3 failed @351/553/792 -> migrated @248/453/695

removed at the top, then 3 added at each call site as the file progresses. Same assertions, same

All four pre-existing failures are downstream product concerns: a cross-window semantic preview the

* docs(testing): the option AC-7b sends the next caller to is documented where they land (#18682)

`placeBesideSource` accepts `envelope` and returns `stageTrusted`; neither
appeared in its docblock. #18682's AC-7b tells a future caller needing a
declared-bounds pin to extend "placeBesideSource's existing envelope option" —
pointing them at a parameter the signature had and the documentation did not.

The docblock now states when to declare an envelope (an emulated page reports a
stage its real windows never occupy) and what a false `stageTrusted` means: the
arrangement was proven by measurement rather than by a fit test.

* fix(testing): a no-move verdict answers only for a stage it actually checked (#18682)

`placeBesideSource` decided the stage authority AFTER its settle loop, so the
no-move path answered first and answered wrongly: two windows that merely miss
each other returned `fits: true, stageTrusted: true` without ever consulting the
envelope the caller declared. @neo-gpt-emmy's probe on PR #18698 — source at
20,0 760x700, target at 820,0 600x500, envelope 800x720 — took that path and
called a target reaching x=1420 a fit on an 800-wide stage, reaching no CDP
session to find out otherwise. An emulated page with no envelope claimed trust
the same way.

That is this module's own defect turned inward: a verdict asserting a stage it
had not measured is exactly what #18682 exists to remove from the suite.

The authority is now decided before any verdict, and containment is three-valued
so that "cannot be established" can never read as "yes". Apart is necessary and
no longer sufficient — a target parked outside a declared envelope falls through
to be placed instead of being kept — and `stageTrusted` reports what was actually
established. The contract states what a `fits` verdict does and does not promise:
non-overlap always, display containment only when the stage was trusted.

Two red-first arms at her exact numbers, plus the 1600-wide control that must
keep answering no-move; 19/19."
